key_insight: Replace reconstruction-oriented latent decoders with a conditional pixel-space diffusion decoder (PiD) that synthesizes high-frequency detail directly from compact latents, enabling faster and higher-resolution image reconstruction at megapixel scale.
problem_solved: Latent-to-pixel decoders are optimized to invert encoders and become computationally expensive and detail-poor at megapixel resolutions; PiD addresses the need for a more expressive, efficient decoder that produces richer high-resolution images.
method: Introduce PiD: a pixel diffusion decoder conditioned on compact latent codes so the model synthesizes fine details instead of strictly reconstructing encoder outputs.
Scale to megapixel images with efficiency tactics such as multi-scale/patch-wise diffusion, parallel sampling strategies and compute-aware scheduling to reduce memory and latency.
Train with perceptual/high-frequency-focused objectives and conditioning strategies to enable fewer sampling steps while preserving visual fidelity.
impact: Enables practitioners to decode large, high-quality images faster and with lower compute cost—making high-resolution text-to-image and latent-generation pipelines more practical for production and research.

paper_title: PiD: Fast and High-Resolution Latent Decoding with Pixel Diffusion
paper_authors: Yifan Lu, Qi Wu, Jay Zhangjie Wu, Zian Wang, Huan Ling
